title: Odd and Even Numbers Worksheets Within 20
intro: Use pairs to explain odd and even numbers.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Arrange counters in pairs. Discuss whether every counter has a partner before naming the number odd or even.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

8 = 4 + 4

Place one counter from each pair in a left-hand group and its partner in a right-hand group. Both groups contain four counters. An even total can be written as two equal whole-number addends.

Ask your student

Is there a counter left without a partner?

If your student needs help

If the student guesses from appearance, rearrange the counters and pair them again.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet has two classification questions, two draw-pairs questions, and two equal-addend questions. Numbers are from 1 through 20. A number may reappear in a different activity, and a set does not guarantee an equal number of odd and even examples.
